reproducibility_gaps: Final Stage 2 verified the public GitLab project and master branch but did not expose a 40-character commit SHA or repository tree, so the closed Stage-2 state does not define an immutable source snapshot.
PyPI 1.0.2 supplies immutable source/wheel hashes, but Stage 3 did not compare those package bytes with a GitLab revision and does not assert repository-release byte equality.

TensorFlow compatibility changed across generations: the 2021 paper reports >=2.4, PyPI 1.0.1 reports 2.4-2.10, while the 2025 maintenance update targets newer TensorFlow and states incompatibility with older versions around 2.10 while leaving CI TensorFlow unpinned.
No complete exact transitive dependency lock or immutable container environment is established by the provider surfaces inspected.

The complete current GitLab source tree was not exposed through the bounded primary-source interface used here; implementation details beyond paper/documentation/package/provider metadata remain source-tree bounded.
Elvet is a reusable framework rather than one fixed application; no canonical dataset, seed, experiment configuration, checkpoint or expected result is defined at resource scope.
Examples, Colab notebooks, tests, provider pipelines, training and prediction were not executed under the Stage-3 static-only boundary.
notes: R2 is assigned at reusable-framework scope because public source identity, MIT licensing, versioned PyPI source artifacts, installation instructions, API, mathematical method, architecture/training behavior, examples and evaluation interfaces are statically recoverable.
R3 is withheld because no authoritative Stage-2 source commit exists, repository/release lineage was not byte-compared, TensorFlow generations conflict, and no exact transitive environment is fixed.
The provider-reported passing 2025 pipeline is evidence of provider testing only; Stage 3 did not re-run it.
